36|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
37|# 1. BPE Token Estimator & Fast JSON
38|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
39|_SAMPLE_CHARS = 8192
40|_SAMPLE_THRESHOLD = 65536
41|_BPE_PAT = re.compile(
42|    r"'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d| ?\w+| ?\d+| ?[^\s\w\d]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+"
43|)
44|

46|def fast_json_loads(data: str | bytes) -> Any:
47|    """Fastest available JSON deserializer (msgspec > jiter > stdlib json)."""
48|    if _MSGSPEC_AVAILABLE:
49|        try:
50|            raw = data if isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)) else data.encode("utf-8")
51|            return msgspec.json.decode(raw)
52|        except Exception:
53|            pass
54|    if _JITER_AVAILABLE:
55|        try:
56|            if isinstance(data, str):
57|                return jiter.from_json(data.encode("utf-8"))
58|            return jiter.from_json(data)
59|        except Exception:
60|            pass
61|    if isinstance(data, bytes):
62|        return json.loads(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
63|    return json.loads(data)
64|
65|
66|def estimate_bpe_tokens(text: str) -> int:
67|    """Approximate or exact BPE token count. Never raises; 0 for non-str/empty."""
68|    try:
69|        if not text or not isinstance(text, str):
70|            return 0
71|        if _TOKENIZER is not None:
72|            if len(text) > _SAMPLE_THRESHOLD:
73|                sample = text[:_SAMPLE_CHARS]
74|                count = len(_TOKENIZER.encode_ordinary(sample))
75|                return max(1, int(len(text) * (count / _SAMPLE_CHARS)))
76|            return len(_TOKENIZER.encode_ordinary(text))
77|        if len(text) > _SAMPLE_THRESHOLD:
78|            sample = text[:_SAMPLE_CHARS]
79|            ratio = len(_BPE_PAT.findall(sample)) / _SAMPLE_CHARS
80|            return max(1, int(len(text) * ratio))
81|        return len(_BPE_PAT.findall(text))
82|    except Exception:
83|        return 0
84|
85|
86|def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
87|    """Standard token estimator interface."""
88|    return estimate_bpe_tokens(text)
89|
90|
91|def estimate_bpe_gain(before: str, after: str) -> int:
92|    """Token gain of a fold (before - after); >0 means the fold is worth it."""
93|    return estimate_bpe_tokens(before) - estimate_bpe_tokens(after)

103|_ERROR_RE = re.compile(
104|    r"(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])|[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:Error|Exception)\b)"
105|    r"(?:error(?:s)?|exception|traceback|fail(?:ed|ure|s)?|panic(?:ked)?|fatal|critical|"
106|    r"warn(?:ing|ings)?|denied|refused|timeout|seg(?:fault|mentation\s+fault)|"
107|    r"sig(?:segv|abrt|bus|kill|term)|undefined\s+reference|killed|"
108|    r"assert(?:ion)?(?:error|ion|\s+failed)?|oom(?:killed)?|npm\s+err!|epipe|"
109|    r"exit\s+(?:code|status)\s+[1-9]\d*|out\s+of\s+memory|"
110|    r"status(?:_code)?[=:\s]+5\d{2}(?![0-9])|"
111|    r"http[/\d.\s]*5\d{2}(?![0-9])|bad\s+gateway|"
112|    r"ข้อผิดพลาด|ผิดพลาด|ล้มเหลว|ขัดข้อง)"
113|    r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])"
114|    r"|\b[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:Error|Exception|Fault|Panic):"
115|    r"|^\s*(?:File |  at |Caused by:|\d+:\s+0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)",
116|    re.I,
117|)
118|
119|_ERROR_HINTS = (
120|    "error", "exception", "traceback", "fail", "panic", "fatal", "critical",
121|    "warn", "denied", "refused", "timeout", "segfault", "segmentation", "fault",
122|    "assert", "oom", "epipe", "exit code", "exit status", "out of memory",
123|    "oomkilled", "npm err!", "bad gateway", "undefined reference", "killed", "sigsegv", "sigabrt",
124|    "sigbus", "sigkill", "sigterm",
125|    "ผิดพลาด", "ล้มเหลว", "ขัดข้อง", "ข้อผิดพลาด",
126|    "file ", "  at ", "caused by:",
127|)
128|
129|# Loose hints ("status", "http", "sig", "memory") sent ~every info log line into
130|# the 614-char _ERROR_RE (~42us/line, 1.3s on a 20K-line dump). These three are
131|# the same checks with their literal prefix asserted first: the prefilter stays a
132|# strict superset of _ERROR_RE, so nothing is dropped and the precise regex still
133|# decides.
134|_STATUS5_RE = re.compile(r"status(?:_code)?[=:\s]+5\d{2}(?![0-9])", re.I)
135|_HTTP5_RE = re.compile(r"http[/\d.\s]*5\d{2}(?![0-9])", re.I)
136|_HEX_FRAME_RE = re.compile(r"\d+:\s+0x[0-9a-fA-F]+")
137|
138|
139|def looks_suspicious(low: str) -> bool:
140|    """Cheap reject-before-expensive-regex prefilter (never rejects a real fault)."""
141|    for h in _ERROR_HINTS:
142|        if h in low:
143|            return True
144|    if "status" in low and _STATUS5_RE.search(low):
145|        return True
146|    if "http" in low and _HTTP5_RE.search(low):
147|        return True
148|    if "0x" in low and _HEX_FRAME_RE.search(low):
149|        return True
150|    return False
151|

153|_CACHEABLE_MAX_CHARS = 240
154|_FAULT_CACHE_SIZE = 16384
155|
156|# Negated / concept phrases that mention fault words but are NOT faults
157|# ("no error", "0 warnings", "error-handling policy"). Stripped before the real
158|# check so a benign mention does not lock a line as important, which would
159|# defeat compression on ordinary info logs (F1). A real error signal on the
160|# same line is untouched, so genuine errors are still detected.
161|_BENIGN_RE = re.compile(
162|    r"(?:no\s+(?:error|errors|warning|warnings|warn|warns|failure|failures|fail|fails|"
163|    r"exception|exceptions|fault|faults|panic|panics|assertion|assertions|"
164|    r"issue|issues|problem|problems|crash|crashes)"
165|    r"|(?:0|zero)\s+(?:error|errors|warning|warnings|warn|warns|failure|failures|"
166|    r"exception|exceptions|issue|issues|problem|problems)"
167|    r"|without\s+(?:error|errors|warning|warnings|warn|warns|failure|failures))"
168|    r"|error[- ](?:handling|policy|recovery|detection|reporting|checking|"
169|    r"tracking|summary|count|counts|free|bound|bounds|tolerant|correction)",
170|    re.I,
171|)
172|
173|
174|def _compute_fault(line: str) -> bool:
175|    if not line:
176|        return False
177|    if not looks_suspicious(line.lower()):
178|        return False
179|    # Strip negated/concept phrases first so "no error" / "error-handling"
180|    # do not falsely lock a benign line as a fault (F1).
181|    probe = _BENIGN_RE.sub(" ", line)
182|    return bool(_ERROR_RE.search(probe))
183|
184|
185|_cached_fault = lru_cache(maxsize=_FAULT_CACHE_SIZE)(_compute_fault)
186|
187|
188|def is_fault_line(line: str) -> bool:
189|    if not line:
190|        return False
191|    if len(line) <= _CACHEABLE_MAX_CHARS:
192|        return _cached_fault(line)
193|    return _compute_fault(line)

226|def is_important(line: str) -> bool:
227|    """True when a line contains an error, exception, or failure indicator."""
228|    if not line:

251|def adaptive_terminal_head(
252|    kind: str,
253|    omitted_lines: int,
254|    digest: str,
255|    raw_len: int,
256|    gross_saved_chars: int,
257|    legend: str = LEGEND_FOLD,
258|    *,
259|    force_tier: int | None = None,
260|) -> list[str]:
261|    """Return header lines scaled to payload size and savings (Tier 0..3).
262|
263|    Tier 0: omitted_lines == 0 (lossless hygiene/ANSI strip only) -> [] (0 chars)
264|    Tier 1: small payload AND small saving -> 1-line nano tag (~18 chars)
265|    Tier 2: medium payload AND moderate saving -> 1-line compact tag (~60 chars)
266|    Tier 3: everything else -> full terminal_head + legend (~165 chars)
267|
268|    NOTE (v4.2): the plan (TRIMTOK_V4_ARGON_PLAN.md 4.1) spells the tier test as
269|    ``raw_len <= 4096 or gross_saved_chars < 240``.  That literal reading makes
270|    the header depend on payload size ONLY: every payload <= 4096 chars would
271|    drop the legend, which silently changes the long-standing v4.1 wire format
272|    (tests/test_core.py asserts ``out.startswith("[tt:terminal")`` and that the
273|    second line is exactly LEGEND_FOLD).  The plan's own docstring says the
274|    header is "scaled to payload size AND savings", and the telemetry goal is
275|    only to avoid a header that eats the saving, so the two conditions are
276|    combined with AND here: a small header is used when the saving is small
277|    (that is the 2KB-4KB band that produced 558 reverted_gate events), and the
278|    full header is kept whenever the saving comfortably pays for it.
279|    """
280|    if omitted_lines <= 0 and force_tier is None:
281|        return []
282|    ref = digest if digest.startswith("#") else f"#{digest}"
283|    tier = force_tier
284|    if tier is None:
285|        # Driven by the SAVING, not by the payload size: a 10 KB payload that only
286|        # saved 100 chars must not carry a 165-char header (that is the band that
287|        # produced the reverted_gate failures).
288|        if gross_saved_chars < 240:
289|            tier = 1
290|        elif gross_saved_chars < 450:
291|            tier = 2
292|        else:
293|            tier = 3
294|
295|    if tier <= 0:
296|        return []
297|    if tier == 1:
298|        return [f"[tt:{ref} -{omitted_lines}L]"]
299|    if tier == 2:
300|        return [f"[tt:{kind} -{omitted_lines}L {ref} | retrieve(hash=\"{ref}\", section=\"errors|diff|tail\")]"]
301|    return [terminal_head(kind, omitted_lines, digest.lstrip("#")), legend]
302|
303|
304|def adaptive_tool_head(
305|    saved_chars: int,
306|    digest: str,
307|    raw_len: int,
308|    *,
309|    is_lossless_only: bool = False,
310|    force_tier: int | None = None,
311|) -> str:
312|    """Return tool header scaled to payload size and lossiness (Tier 0..3).
313|
314|    Tier 0: nothing was removed (lossless-only result) -> "" (no header)
315|    Tier 1: 1-line nano tag (~18 chars)
316|    Tier 2: 1-line compact tag with a retrieve() hint (~60 chars)
317|    Tier 3: full tool_head with kind/saved/ref (~45 chars)
318|    """
319|    if is_lossless_only and force_tier is None:
320|        return ""
321|    ref = digest if digest.startswith("#") else f"#{digest}"
322|    tier = force_tier
323|    if tier is None:
324|        # Saving-driven, like adaptive_terminal_head: a small saving must not
325|        # carry a header bigger than the saving.
326|        if saved_chars < 240:
327|            tier = 1
328|        elif saved_chars < 450:
329|            tier = 2
330|        else:
331|            tier = 3
332|
333|    if tier <= 0:
334|        return ""
335|    if tier == 1:
336|        return f"[tt:{ref} -{saved_chars}c]"                                        # ~18 chars
337|    if tier == 2:
338|        return tool_head(saved_chars, digest.lstrip("#"))                           # ~45 chars
339|    return f"[tt:tool kind=result saved={saved_chars} {ref} | retrieve(hash=\"{ref}\")]"  # ~68 chars

367|    r"(?i)port\s+\d{2,5}|(?<!\d):\d{2,5}\b|[0-9a-f]{7,40}|"

378|    try:
379|        if (line or "").startswith("TRIMTOK_KEEP:"):

387|# 4. Guard & ANSI Utilities

389|VERBATIM_TOOLS = frozenset({"read_file", "write_to_file", "replace_file_content", "ask_question"})
390|# Read tools whose payload is a numbered file body: the stateful file engine
391|# handles them, so they are NOT verbatim-only.

394|_ANSI_RE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]|\x1b\][^\x07]*\x07|\x1b[()][AB0]")

397|def strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
398|    if "\x1b" not in text and "\x9b" not in text:
399|        return text
400|    return _ANSI_RE.sub("", text)

403|class Deadline:
404|    """Monotonic deadline guard with configurable budget."""
405|
406|    def __init__(self, budget_ms: float = 50.0) -> None:
407|        self.budget_ms = max(1.0, budget_ms)
408|        self.deadline = time.monotonic() + (self.budget_ms / 1000.0)
409|
410|    def check(self) -> None:
411|        if time.monotonic() > self.deadline:
412|            raise TimeoutError(f"Trimtok deadline exceeded ({self.budget_ms:.1f}ms)")
